case.title: The Meridian File - fictional training case
case.question: Who can influence the proposed compute-licensing rule, through which actual mechanisms, and what would distinguish funder direction from coordinated or independent agreement?
case.scope: Entirely fictional people, organizations, events, documents, amounts, and quotations. Teach investigative distinctions; this is not evidence about real actors.
case.notes: Start with Cobalt -> Meridian -> licensing rule. Inspect the narrow approval right, compare the reporting ancestry, and filter appointments by year. Removing Cobalt tests visible connectivity only; the surviving Mira -> review panel -> Standards Office path merits role-specific inquiry, not a claim of control. All source locators refer to invented teaching records summarized here; no external documents are claimed to exist.

priors.statement: I suspect a shared patron is synchronizing both the institute and the incumbent lab. Preserve this as my starting hypothesis while testing mechanisms.

journal.change: Preserved a direction allegation from three publications, provisionally as reported.
Traced all three publications to one grant announcement. Marked broad direction disputed; retained the separate documented approval right over Meridian's funded brief.
Appointment dates refuted simultaneous employment; retained the retracted assertion for audit and continued investigating the later advisory role.
Added explicit analytical dependencies, multi-parent correction ancestry, editorial view curation and a resumable fictional collection frontier. All original teaching facts and statuses are retained.

campaign.resume: The July packet cannot explain the June endorsement. Seek an earlier authorized recipient record; retain the later bounded revision channel and compare independent incentives.

hypotheses.title: Broad patron direction
hypotheses.statement: Cobalt synchronized both Meridian and Astera's campaign through a common command arrangement.
hypotheses.prior: Fictional requester: strong starting suspicion; retain as an attributed hypothesis.
assumptions: Cobalt had a route to direct Astera beyond its Meridian grant.
The similar policy positions reflect that route rather than separate incentives.
predictions: Instructions or approval records should connect Cobalt to Astera before its submission.
A shared private draft should precede the public positions.
hypotheses.next_test: Obtain the relevant correspondence or recipient register through an authorized route; copied articles are insufficient.
hypotheses.alternative: Cobalt exercised bounded rights over one Meridian deliverable while Astera supported the proposal for its own reasons.

hypotheses.title: Bounded grant control plus parallel incentives
hypotheses.statement: Cobalt shaped Meridian's funded brief through explicit limited rights, while Astera independently favored a rule compatible with its constraints.
assumptions: The supplied contract scope is materially complete.
Astera's position does not require a hidden instruction to make strategic sense.
predictions: Meridian's revisions should track in-scope liaison requests.
Astera's earlier policy rationale may predate any alleged shared briefing.
hypotheses.next_test: Compare Astera's pre-consultation statements with dated revision records; inspect any separate agreement if discovered.
hypotheses.alternative: A shared briefing channel coordinated positions despite the absence of broad funder command.

hypotheses.title: Shared briefing channel without a central controller
hypotheses.statement: An intermediary distributed a common packet that helped coordinate positions across organizations, without requiring Cobalt to command Astera.
assumptions: Astera received materially similar nonpublic material before its relevant policy statements.
Shared-venue contact led to transmission rather than merely co-presence.
predictions: Recipient records should include an Astera contact, with a date that can precede the position being explained.
Distinctive edits or shared errors should appear across the relevant drafts.
hypotheses.next_test: Check packet recipients and timestamps. Astera's 2025-06-01 endorsement predates the documented 2025-07-02 packet, so this packet cannot explain that initial endorsement.
hypotheses.alternative: Participants independently used public consultation material; the packet only coordinated Meridian's later revisions.

leads.question: Did any separate instrument extend Cobalt's rights beyond this specific brief?
leads.rationale: A narrower documented right cannot establish broader command; a second agreement would materially change the mechanism map.
leads.expected_observation: An authenticated additional agreement or direction record connecting Cobalt and Astera.
leads.alternative_result: A scoped search yields only the bounded Meridian agreement; report coverage and access limits, not universal absence.
leads.record_type: Signed agreement, amendment or approval clause
leads.query: Exact parties, instrument ID and approval scope before the consultation

leads.question: Who received the packet, and when?
leads.rationale: Recipient and timing evidence can distinguish a shared coordination channel from independent convergence.
leads.expected_observation: Authorized recipient register and version timestamps.
leads.alternative_result: No pre-endorsement delivery is established; the July packet cannot cause Astera's June endorsement.
leads.record_type: Recipient register and versioned briefing packet
leads.query: Astera recipient and authenticated timestamp before 2025-06-01

leads.question: Do the three direction reports provide independent observations?
leads.rationale: Source volume can inflate an allegation when all outlets repeat one origin.
leads.answer: No independent observation is present in the teaching records. The chain leads back to a grant announcement about Meridian.

leads.question: What recommendations did Mira's review panel actually send to the agency?
leads.rationale: Removing the funder leaves a public-role access path whose concrete output matters more than mere connectivity.
leads.expected_observation: Dated recommendations, authorship records, and agency treatment of the advice.
leads.alternative_result: Attendance without attributable advice, or agency rejection, narrows the influence claim.
leads.custodian: Public Procurement Unit or Standards Office
leads.query: Technical review panel recommendations submitted in the 2025 consultation

leads.question: Was service dependence used to exert policy pressure?
leads.rationale: Suspension capability and switching costs may create leverage, but exercise is unobserved.
leads.expected_observation: Revive only if authorized correspondence, a service dispute, or a direct account links supply conditions to the policy position.
leads.alternative_result: Ordinary service administration consistent with the existing terms; do not expand merely because the supplier is important.
leads.custodian: Authorized contract or service-dispute record custodian
leads.query: Authenticated link between Cloudspan supply conditions and the policy position

games.title: The brief, the renewal, and the incumbent
games.summary: A qualitative conditional model: Cobalt and Meridian bargain within a funded deliverable's scope; Astera has an independent policy position and compute constraints. No common payoff function, hidden agreement, or equilibrium is asserted.

players.objective: Obtain the agreed research deliverable in a form the liaison approves.
players.basis: s-agreement section 4 and s-revisions; broader political aims remain inferred.
constraints: Approval is limited to the named brief and scope.
Payments already due are not automatically discretionary.
outside_options: Fund a different future research project, subject to existing obligations.

players.objective: Publish the research and maintain organizational resources.
players.basis: Documented authorship and funding; the preference for renewal is an explicit model assumption.
constraints: Institutional credibility can be damaged by undisclosed outside direction.
outside_options: Publish separate unfunded work consistent with actual agreements.

players.objective: Support a workable licensing framework while retaining market access.
players.basis: s-consultation; an incumbent advantage from fixed costs is an analytical inference, not a statement of secret motive.
constraints: The supplied service contract permits suspension only on specified grounds.
moves: Participate in a documented coalition if one is established.

sequence: Grant and review rights are agreed in January.
Astera endorses the proposal on June 1.
Meridian's revision packet is sent July 2 and its brief is submitted July 15.

scenarios.label: Bounded revision, independent endorsement
assumptions: Approval stays inside the contract scope.
Astera's independent rationale is sufficient to explain its position.
implications: Compatible positions need no shared controller.

scenarios.label: A genuine shared channel
assumptions: An earlier nonpublic packet or meeting is established.
The common material reached the relevant decision makers before the position being explained.
implications: Some coordination may be supported without broad patron command.

scenarios.label: Pressure beyond the agreement
assumptions: A credible threat connects a resource decision to out-of-scope policy demands.
The recipient lacks a timely substitute.
implications: Practical leverage may exceed formal approval rights, but this requires new evidence.
signals: Subsequent response consistent with that specific threat.
